To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

binding to albumin is a determinant of serum concentration and elimination rate; binding to cell membranes is a determinant of distribution in tissues, including the penetration into areas of inflammation; binding to intracellular proteins is a determinant of intracellular concentrations and elimination rate; and binding to insoluble intracellular materials is a determinant of penetration of the drug into the cell.
the pharmacologic activity of an antibiotic depends upon its ability to bind to the target site and that binding to serum albumin is a prerequisite for the antibiotic to reach the site of action.

1. binding to serum albumin has a profound influence on distribution, elimination, and biologic effects; 2. binding to membranes and intracellular proteins is important in the distribution of the drug in the body; and 3. binding to insoluble materials is an important mechanism of inactivation of drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of binding of antibiotics to serum proteins, cell membranes, intracellular proteins, and intracellular insoluble substances, and the effects on the pharmacologic activity of the antibiotic.
the effect of binding on pharmacologic activity of antibiotics, with the goal of understanding the mechanism of action of these drugs.
the effect of binding on the disposition and activity of antibiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
binding is a complex phenomenon which is difficult to evaluate.
the pharmacokinetics of an antibiotic is a function of its affinity for the various types of binding sites, and that the biologic activity is a function of the concentration at the site of action.
binding to serum proteins, cell membranes, intracellular proteins and insoluble intracellular material may alter the distribution and elimination rates of antibiotics and their biologic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of binding on pharmacokinetics and activity is complex and variable.

binding to albumin is a major determinant of serum concentrations of antibiotics and that binding to cell membranes and intracellular proteins may be a major determinant of tissue concentrations and activity.
the binding of antibiotics to serum proteins is a major factor influencing serum concentrations, tissue penetration, and distribution in the body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotics are not all the same.
the binding characteristics of an antibiotic can have a profound effect on its pharmacokinetics, distribution, penetration into tissues and organs, and activity.
the biologic activity of an antibiotic may depend more on its binding than on the serum concentration of the antibiotic.
